name: Strait of Hormuz
genZNote: A big chunk of the world's oil passes through a gap narrow enough that it makes the news every time there's regional tension. That's Hormuz.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A natural strait between Iran to the north and Oman (via its Musandam exclave) to the south.
Connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, and from there to the Arabian Sea and the wider Indian Ocean.
One of the narrowest points ships have to pass through on this route — narrow enough that shipping lanes are tightly regulated within it.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: The single most important oil chokepoint in the world by volume — a very large share of the world's seaborne crude oil exports passes through it, mostly from Gulf producers (Saudi Arabia, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Iran).
Any disruption here has an outsized effect on global oil prices, which is why it is closely watched during periods of regional tension.
Nearby countries: Iran, Oman, and (further along the Gulf) Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 India Connection
bullets: The majority of India's crude oil imports from the Gulf pass through the Strait of Hormuz on their way across the Arabian Sea to Indian ports.
Any disruption to shipping through Hormuz is a direct energy-security concern for India, given how much of its oil supply transits this one point.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman/Arabian Sea, and is the world's single most important oil-shipping chokepoint.
keyFacts: Connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.
World's most important chokepoint for seaborne oil trade.
Most of India's Gulf oil imports pass through it.
commonConfusion: Don't confuse the Strait of Hormuz (Persian Gulf exit) with the Strait of Malacca (a completely different chokepoint near Southeast Asia).

highYieldFacts: Hormuz connects Persian Gulf ↔ Gulf of Oman ↔ Arabian Sea.
commonTraps: A strait is a natural channel — don't call Hormuz a canal (canals like Suez/Panama are man-made).
mustRemember: Hormuz = Persian Gulf's only sea exit; world's top oil chokepoint; critical for India's energy imports.
